anchor.exact: Ainu marks person and number with verbal affixes, which are obligatory.

statement.en: In Ainu, person and number are obligatorily marked on the verb by verbal affixes.
statement.ja: アイヌ語では、人称と数が動詞接辞によって動詞上に義務的に標示される。

entailment.quote: Ainu marks person and number with verbal affixes, which are obligatory.

anchor.exact: There are also personal pronouns, and personal pronouns and adverbial particles may be placed before the verb; see examples (3) and (4) in Bugaeva (Chapter 1, this volume), but even in such cases, person affixes are attached to the verb.

statement.en: Personal pronouns and adverbial particles may precede the verb, but person affixes remain attached to the verb even when an independent personal pronoun is present.
statement.ja: 人称代名詞や副詞的粒子は動詞の前に置かれうるが、人称代名詞が存在する場合でも動詞には人称接辞が付加される。

entailment.quote: personal pronouns and adverbial particles may be placed before the verb; ... but even in such cases, person affixes are attached to the verb.

anchor.exact: The use of a personal pronoun may deliberately stress the subject, but normally a subject is expressed by the person affixes alone.

statement.en: A subject in Ainu is normally expressed by verbal person affixes alone, whereas an overt personal pronoun is used to deliberately stress the subject.
statement.ja: アイヌ語の主語は通常は人称接辞のみで表現され、人称代名詞の使用は主語を意図的に強調する場合に限られる。

entailment.quote: The use of a personal pronoun may deliberately stress the subject, but normally a subject is expressed by the person affixes alone.

anchor.exact: Since third person is expressed by a zero affix, if an overt affix does not appear, it is interpreted as third person.

statement.en: Third person in Ainu is expressed by a zero affix, so a verb form without an overt person affix is interpreted as third person.
statement.ja: アイヌ語の3人称はゼロ接辞で表されるため、明示的な人称接辞が現れない場合は3人称と解釈される。

entailment.quote: Since third person is expressed by a zero affix, if an overt affix does not appear, it is interpreted as third person.

anchor.exact: Also, no prefix can appear before a person-affix prefix and no suffix can appear after a person-affix suffix. Thus, when such prefixes or suffixes are affixed, the presence of a word boundary can be determined.

statement.en: No prefix can precede a person-affix prefix and no suffix can follow a person-affix suffix, making person affixes diagnostic of the verb word boundary.
statement.ja: 人称接頭辞の前に接頭辞が現れることはなく、人称接尾辞の後に接尾辞が現れることもないため、これらにより動詞の語境界を判定できる。

entailment.quote: no prefix can appear before a person-affix prefix and no suffix can appear after a person-affix suffix. Thus, when such prefixes or suffixes are affixed, the presence of a word boundary can be determined.

anchor.exact: Thus, one can clearly distinguish in Ainu whether a verb is 1-argument or 2/3-argument by means of what person affixes are attached.

statement.en: Whether an Ainu verb is a 1-argument verb versus a 2- or 3-argument verb is clearly distinguished by which set of subject person affixes attaches to it.
statement.ja: アイヌ語の動詞が1項動詞であるか2/3項動詞であるかは、どの人称接辞が付加されるかによって明確に区別される。

entailment.quote: one can clearly distinguish in Ainu whether a verb is 1-argument or 2/3-argument by means of what person affixes are attached.

anchor.exact: For example, if the subject is first-person plural exclusive, the 1-argument verb inkar ‘see/look’ will have the suffix -as attached as in inkar-as ‘we (EXCL) see’, and the 2-argument verb nukar ‘see sth’ will have the prefix ci- attached as in ci-nukar ‘we (EXCL) see it’.

statement.en: In the Saru dialect, the first-person plural exclusive subject of a 1-argument verb is marked by the suffix -as, whereas the subject of a 2-argument or 3-argument verb is marked by the prefix ci-.
statement.ja: 沙流方言において、1項動詞の1人称複数除外の主語は接尾辞 -as で標示されるのに対し、2項または3項動詞の主語は接頭辞 ci- で標示される。

entailment.quote: if the subject is first-person plural exclusive, the 1-argument verb inkar ... will have the suffix -as ... and the 2-argument verb nukar ... will have the prefix ci-

anchor.exact: | Fourth-Person            | -an             | a-              | i-                    |

statement.en: In the Saru dialect, the fourth-person subject of a 1-argument verb is marked by the suffix -an, whereas the fourth-person subject of a 2- or 3-argument verb is marked by the prefix a-.
statement.ja: 沙流方言において、1項動詞の4人称主語は接尾辞 -an で標示されるのに対し、2項・3項動詞の4人称主語は接頭辞 a- で標示される。

entailment.quote: Fourth-Person | -an | a- | i-

anchor.exact: | Fourth-Person            | -an             | a-              | i-                    |

statement.en: In the Saru dialect, the fourth-person object is marked on the verb by the prefix i-.
statement.ja: 沙流方言において、4人称の目的語は動詞上で接頭辞 i- によって標示される。

entailment.quote: Fourth-Person ... i-

statement.en: In the Saru dialect, second-person singular is marked by e- for both subjects (1-, 2-, and 3-argument verbs) and objects, and second-person plural is marked by eci- for both subjects and objects.
statement.ja: 沙流方言において、2人称単数は主語（1項、2項、3項動詞）および目的語の双方で e- によって標示され、2人称複数も主語および目的語の双方で eci- によって標示される。

entailment.quote: Second-Person | Singular | e- ... Plural | eci-

anchor.exact: | First-Person  | Singular | ku-                               | en-                   |

statement.en: In the Saru dialect, first-person singular subject is marked by ku- across 1-argument, 2-argument, and 3-argument verbs, and first-person singular object is marked by en-.
statement.ja: 沙流方言において、1人称単数主語は1項・2項・3項動詞を通じて ku- で標示され、1人称単数目的語は en- で標示される。

entailment.quote: First-Person | Singular | ku- ... en-

anchor.exact: | First-Person  | ... | Plural   | -as             | ci-             | un-                   |

statement.en: In the Saru dialect, first-person plural object is marked by the prefix un-.
statement.ja: 沙流方言において、1人称複数目的語は接頭辞 un- で標示される。

anchor.exact: there are verbs for which, without a change in the number of arguments, there are alternations in the semantic roles the arguments play.

statement.en: Some Ainu verbs exhibit uncoded alternations in the semantic roles of their arguments without a change in syntactic valency (the number of arguments).
statement.ja: アイヌ語の動詞の中には、統語的価項数（項の数）が変化することなく、項の果たす意味役割が交替するものが存在する。

entailment.quote: there are verbs for which, without a change in the number of arguments, there are alternations in the semantic roles the arguments play

anchor.exact: 1-argument verbs may take any of Agent, Theme, or Space/Location as subjects.

statement.en: One-argument verbs in Ainu can take an Agent, a Theme, or a Space/Location as their subject.
statement.ja: アイヌ語の1項動詞は、動作主、起点/対象（Theme）、または空間/場所を主語として取ることができる。

entailment.quote: 1-argument verbs may take any of Agent, Theme, or Space/Location as subjects

anchor.exact: 1-arguments verbs that take an Agent as subject include ones like apkas ‘walk’ and yapkir ‘throw’.

statement.en: The one-argument verbs apkas 'walk' and yapkir 'throw' take an Agent as their subject.
statement.ja: 1項動詞 apkas「歩く」や yapkir「投げる」は動作主を主語に取る。

entailment.quote: 1-arguments verbs that take an Agent as subject include ones like apkas ‘walk’ and yapkir ‘throw’

anchor.exact: Verbs that take Themes as subjects include ones like makke ‘open’ and tuy ‘break/get cut’.

statement.en: The one-argument verbs makke 'open' and tuy 'break/get cut' take a Theme as their subject.
statement.ja: 1項動詞 makke「開く」や tuy「折れる、切れる」は対象（Theme）を主語に取る。

entailment.quote: Verbs that take Themes as subjects include ones like makke ‘open’ and tuy ‘break/get cut’

anchor.exact: Those that take Space/Location as subjects include peker ‘be bright’ and hutne ‘be narrow/constricted’.

statement.en: The one-argument verbs peker 'be bright' and hutne 'be narrow/constricted' take a Space/Location as their subject.
statement.ja: 1項動詞 peker「明るい」や hutne「狭い」は空間/場所を主語に取る。

entailment.quote: Those that take Space/Location as subjects include peker ‘be bright’ and hutne ‘be narrow/constricted’

anchor.exact: In the case of 2-argument verbs, three types can be identified: verbs that take an Agent and a Theme, verbs that take an Agent and a Space/Location, and verbs that take a Theme and a Space/Location.

statement.en: Two-argument verbs in Ainu fall into three types based on argument roles: Agent and Theme, Agent and Space/Location, or Theme and Space/Location.
statement.ja: アイヌ語の2項動詞には、項の意味役割に基づき、動作主と対象（Theme）、動作主と空間/場所、対象（Theme）と空間/場所の3つのタイプが認められる。

entailment.quote: In the case of 2-argument verbs, three types can be identified: verbs that take an Agent and a Theme, verbs that take an Agent and a Space/Location, and verbs that take a Theme and a Space/Location.

anchor.exact: An example of a verb that takes an Agent as subject and a Theme as object is tuy-e ‘cut sth/sb’.

statement.en: The two-argument verb tuy-e 'cut sth/sb' takes an Agent subject and a Theme object.
statement.ja: 2項動詞 tuy-e「〜を切る」は動作主を主語に、対象（Theme）を目的語に取る。

entailment.quote: An example of a verb that takes an Agent as subject and a Theme as object is tuy-e ‘cut sth/sb’.

anchor.exact: Verbs taking an Agent as subject and Space/Location as object include kus ‘pass through (somewhere)’.

statement.en: The two-argument verb kus 'pass through (somewhere)' takes an Agent subject and a Space/Location object.
statement.ja: 2項動詞 kus「（どこかを）通る」は動作主を主語に、空間/場所を目的語に取る。

entailment.quote: Verbs taking an Agent as subject and Space/Location as object include kus ‘pass through (somewhere)’.

anchor.exact: Finally, oma ‘be located (somewhere)’ is a verb that takes a Theme and Space/Location.

statement.en: The two-argument verb oma 'be located (somewhere)' takes a Theme and a Space/Location argument.
statement.ja: 2項動詞 oma「（どこかに）ある、入っている」は対象（Theme）と空間/場所を項に取る。

entailment.quote: Finally, oma ‘be located (somewhere)’ is a verb that takes a Theme and Space/Location.

anchor.exact: 3-argument verbs take Agent, Theme, and Space/Location arguments.

statement.en: Three-argument verbs take Agent, Theme, and Space/Location arguments.
statement.ja: 3項動詞は動作主、対象（Theme）、空間/場所の項を取る。

entailment.quote: 3-argument verbs take Agent, Theme, and Space/Location arguments.

anchor.exact: There are 1-argument verbs that can take either an Agent or a Theme as subject. An example is as ‘stand’, as shown below.

statement.en: The one-argument verb as 'stand' can take either an Agent or a Theme as its subject.
statement.ja: 1項動詞 as「立つ」は動作主または対象（Theme）のいずれかを主語に取ることができる。

entailment.quote: There are 1-argument verbs that can take either an Agent or a Theme as subject. An example is as ‘stand’.

anchor.exact: when as takes an Agent for its subject, it forms a semantically reflexive (autocausative) structure, and the corresponding 2-argument form is the indirect causative as-te. In contrast, when it takes a Theme as its subject, the corresponding 2-argument form is the direct causative as-i.

statement.en: For the one-argument verb as 'stand', two causative forms exist: direct causative as-i (with suffix -i) corresponding to a Theme subject, and indirect causative as-te (with productive suffix -te) corresponding to an Agent subject.
statement.ja: 1項動詞 as「立つ」には2種類の使役形が存在し、対象（Theme）主語に対応する直接使役形 as-i（接尾辞 -i）と、動作主主語に対応する間接使役形 as-te（生産的接尾辞 -te）がある。

entailment.quote: when as takes an Agent for its subject, ... the corresponding 2-argument form is the indirect causative as-te. In contrast, when it takes a Theme as its subject, the corresponding 2-argument form is the direct causative as-i.

anchor.exact: The base form of a 3-argument verb takes three arguments showing Agent, Theme, and Space/Location as its arguments. The example below uses us-i ‘attach sth to (somewhere)’.

statement.en: The three-argument base verb us-i means 'attach sth to (somewhere)' and takes Agent, Theme, and Space/Location arguments.
statement.ja: 3項動詞の基本形 us-i は「〜を（どこかに）つける」を意味し、動作主、対象（Theme）、空間/場所を項に取る。

entailment.quote: The base form of a 3-argument verb takes three arguments showing Agent, Theme, and Space/Location as its arguments. The example below uses us-i ‘attach sth to (somewhere)’.

anchor.exact: 2-argument verbs that take space/place as an argument have an argument other than space/place that may be realized as Agent in some cases, and as Theme in others. The verb otke presented by Kirikae is included in this type of verb.

statement.en: The two-argument verb otke 'poke, stick into' allows its non-spatial argument to be realized either as an Agent or as a Theme alongside a Space/Location argument.
statement.ja: 2項動詞 otke「刺す、突く」は、空間/場所の項に加えて、もう一方の項が動作主として現れる場合と対象（Theme）として現れる場合がある。

entailment.quote: 2-argument verbs that take space/place as an argument have an argument other than space/place that may be realized as Agent in some cases, and as Theme in others. The verb otke presented by Kirikae is included in this type of verb.

anchor.exact: There are also 2-argument verbs like kuta ‘empty out’, which in addition to <Agent and Space/Location> and <Theme and Space/Location> argument combinations, as in (51) and (52), show an <Agent and Theme> argument combination as in (53) below.

statement.en: The two-argument verb kuta 'empty out' exhibits three argument structures: Agent and Space/Location, Theme and Space/Location, and Agent and Theme.
statement.ja: 2項動詞 kuta「ぶちまける、空にする」は、〈動作主と空間/場所〉、〈対象と空間/場所〉、〈動作主と対象〉という3通りの項構造を示す。

entailment.quote: There are also 2-argument verbs like kuta ‘empty out’, which in addition to <Agent and Space/Location> and <Theme and Space/Location> argument combinations, as in (51) and (52), show an <Agent and Theme> argument combination as in (53) belo

anchor.exact: other 2-argument verbs that take Space/Location as an argument and that can take an additional argument for which multiple semantic roles can be identified include us ‘attach to (somewhere), grow (somewhere), wear (footwear, trousers)’, o ‘enter (some place), board on (something), bear (fruit as a tree)’, oma ‘enter (some place)’, osma ‘enter (some place)’, kam-u/kam-pa ‘cover (some place, something)’, seske ‘block, cover (some place)’, kik ‘bump into (something, some place), strike (something)’, and pici ‘move away (from somewhere), let (something) loose’.

statement.en: The two-argument verbs us, o, oma, osma, kam-u/kam-pa, seske, kik, and pici take Space/Location as an argument and allow their other argument to alternate among multiple semantic roles.
statement.ja: 2項動詞 us、o、oma、osma、kam-u/kam-pa、seske、kik、pici は空間/場所を項に取り、もう一方の項に複数の意味役割が認められる動詞である。

entailment.quote: other 2-argument verbs that take Space/Location as an argument and that can take an additional argument for which multiple semantic roles can be identified include us, o, oma, osma, kam-u/kam-pa, seske, kik, and pici

anchor.exact: 1-argument and 2/3 argument verbs take different personal affixes (in 1PL.EXCL and 4th person only)

anchor.exact: There are double applicatives in e-ko- and ko-e- and extensive applicative object incorporation.

statement.en: Sociatives in uko- and uwe- can be either subject-oriented with a plural subject or object-oriented with a plural object.
statement.ja: uko-およびuwe-による共同態は、複数主語を伴う主語志向か、複数目的語を伴う目的語志向のいずれかになりうる。

entailment.quote: often pose interpretational difficulties in being either subject-oriented (with a plural subject) or object-oriented (with a plural object)

anchor.exact: sociatives can be formed by a cross-linguistically unusual combination of the reciprocal marker u- and causative markers -re/-e/-te or -ka, a combination that is, however, attested in Kabardian (Alpatov, Bugaeva, and Nedjalkov 2007: 1799), and seems to have an emotive coloring.

statement.en: Sociatives can be formed by combining the reciprocal prefix u- with causative suffixes -re/-e/-te or -ka, carrying an emotive coloring.
statement.ja: 共同態は相互接頭辞u-と使役接尾辞-re/-e/-teまたは-kaの結合によって形成されることもあり、感情的ニュアンスを伴う。

entailment.quote: sociatives can be formed by a cross-linguistically unusual combination of the reciprocal marker u- and causative markers -re/-e/-te or -ka ... seems to have an emotive coloring

anchor.exact: there are three applicative markers. All of them are prefixes promoting peripheral participants (like Instrument, Recipient, or Location) to the direct object or just adding a new non-Agentive participant

statement.en: Ainu has three applicative prefixes: e- ('regarding', 'by', 'at'), ko- ('with respect to', 'together with'), and o- ('in', 'toward').
statement.ja: アイヌ語には3つの結合価増加接頭辞（適用辞）e-（〜に関して、〜によって、〜で）、ko-（〜に対して、〜と共に）、o-（〜の中で、〜へ）が存在する。

entailment.quote: there are three applicative markers ... e- ‘regarding’ / ‘by’ / ‘at (a location)’ ... ko- ‘with respect to’ / ‘together with’ ... o- ‘in (a location)’ / ‘toward (a location)’

anchor.exact: Adding these prefixes increases the valency of the verb by one.

statement.en: Adding an applicative prefix increases the valency of the verb by one.
statement.ja: 適用接頭辞を付加すると、動詞の結合価が1つ増加する。

entailment.quote: Adding these prefixes increases the valency of the verb by one.

anchor.exact: they are allowed with almost all verb classes except meteorological, bodily processes, change of state verbs at one edge of the transitivity hierarchy and effective action verbs at the other (Bugaeva 2015a: 838).

statement.en: Applicatives in Ainu are allowed with almost all verb classes except meteorological, bodily process, and change of state verbs at one edge, and effective action verbs at the other.
statement.ja: アイヌ語の適用辞は、一方の極にある気象動詞・身体過程動詞・状態変化動詞、もう一方の極にある効果的動作動詞を除き、ほぼすべての動詞クラスに許容される。

entailment.quote: they are allowed with almost all verb classes except meteorological, bodily processes, change of state verbs at one edge of the transitivity hierarchy and effective action verbs at the other

anchor.exact: Ainu has double applicatives but they are limited toko-e- or e-ko- with ko- encoding Addressee/Recipient and e- Content without any visible difference between the two combinations.

statement.en: Double applicatives in Ainu are limited to combinations of ko-e- or e-ko-, with ko- encoding Addressee/Recipient and e- Content, without any visible difference between the two orders.
statement.ja: アイヌ語の二重適用辞はko-e-またはe-ko-の組み合わせに限られ、ko-が受託者／受取手を、e-が内容を標示し、語順による明確な差異は見られない。

entailment.quote: Ainu has double applicatives but they are limited toko-e- or e-ko- with ko- encoding Addressee/Recipient and e- Content without any visible difference between the two combinations.

anchor.exact: There are productive -re/-e/-te[225]and non-productive -V[226], -ke,and -ka causatives in Ainu.

statement.en: Ainu has productive causatives marked by -re/-e/-te and non-productive causatives marked by -V, -ke, and -ka.
statement.ja: アイヌ語には生産的な使役接尾辞-re/-e/-teと、非生産的な使役接尾辞-V、-ke、-kaが存在する。

entailment.quote: There are productive -re/-e/-te[225]and non-productive -V[226], -ke,and -ka causatives in Ainu.

anchor.exact: a cross-dialectal comparison shows that the causative function of -ka is gradually being replaced by the productive causative -re/-e/-te which came to be used as a default causative marker of both indirect (or distant) and direct

statement.en: Cross-dialectal comparison indicates that the causative function of -ka is gradually being replaced by the productive causative -re/-e/-te as a default marker of both indirect and direct causation.
statement.ja: 方言間比較によれば、-kaの使役機能は生産的な使役接尾辞-re/-e/-teに徐々に取って代わられ、後者が間接的使役と直接的使役の双方を表すデフォルト標識となっている。

entailment.quote: a cross-dialectal comparison shows that the causative function of -ka is gradually being replaced by the productive causative -re/-e/-te which came to be used as a default causative marker of both indirect (or distant) and direct (or contac

anchor.exact: 0-argument meteorological verbs do not allow this type of causativization and are generally resistant to any valency alternations (Bugaeva 2015a: 837).

statement.en: Zero-argument meteorological verbs do not allow productive causativization with -re/-e/-te and are generally resistant to valency alternations.
statement.ja: 0項の気象動詞は-re/-e/-teによる生産的な使役化を許容せず、一般に結合価交替を受け付けない。

entailment.quote: 0-argument meteorological verbs do not allow this type of causativization and are generally resistant to any valency alternations

anchor.exact: except causatives in -ke, which are only derived from 1-argument verbs, all other causative markers may derive causatives from both 1-argument and 2-argument verbs.

statement.en: Non-productive causatives in -ke derive only from 1-argument verbs, whereas -V, -ka, and -re/-e/-te can derive causatives from both 1-argument and 2-argument verbs.
statement.ja: 非生産的な-ke使役動詞は1項動詞からのみ派生するのに対し、-V、-ka、および-re/-e/-teは1項動詞と2項動詞の双方から使役動詞を派生できる。

entailment.quote: except causatives in -ke, which are only derived from 1-argument verbs, all other causative markers may derive causatives from both 1-argument and 2-argument verbs.
entailment.note: Passage does not mention -re/-e/-te in this context; only -V and -ka are covered.

anchor.exact: Causatives from transitives (here direct causatives) result in a double-object construction (6c)

statement.en: Direct causatives formed from transitive verbs yield a double-object construction in Ainu.
statement.ja: 他動詞から派生した直接使役動詞は、アイヌ語において二重目的語構文を形成する。

entailment.quote: Causatives from transitives (here direct causatives) result in a double-object construction

anchor.exact: even more languages disallow double causatives (Kulikov 1993), which is, however, not the case in Ainu (6c).

statement.en: Ainu permits double causatives, in which a causative suffix is added to an already causativized transitive verb stem.
statement.ja: アイヌ語では、既使役化された他動詞語幹に更なる使役接尾辞を付加する二重使役が許容される。

entailment.quote: even more languages disallow double causatives ... which is, however, not the case in Ainu

anchor.exact: direct causee objects can be incorporated as puma ‘wage/charge’ in (7c) and even antipassivized as in (8), but indirect causee objects cannot

statement.en: Direct causee objects can undergo noun incorporation and antipassivization in Ainu, but indirect causee objects cannot.
statement.ja: アイヌ語では直接使役の被使役者目的語は名詞抱合や逆受動態化を受けることができるが、間接使役の被使役者目的語は受けることができない。

entailment.quote: direct causee objects can be incorporated ... and even antipassivized ... but indirect causee objects cannot

anchor.exact: This is a canonical subject-oriented reciprocal construction and it is always intransitivizing. This type of reciprocal is highly productive: they can be formed from both inherent (9c) and derived 2-argument applicative (41), (13) or causative verbs

statement.en: Canonical subject-oriented reciprocal verbs are formed productively with u- from inherent 2-argument verbs or derived applicatives and causatives, and are always intransitivizing.
statement.ja: 典型的な主語指向の相互動詞は、本来的2項動詞または派生適用詞・使役動詞からu-によって生産的に派生され、常に自動詞化する。

entailment.quote: This is a canonical subject-oriented reciprocal construction and it is always intransitivizing. This type of reciprocal is highly productive: they can be formed from both inherent ... and derived 2-argument applicative ... or causative verb
entailment.note: Passage does not explicitly name the u- prefix; it supports the rest of the statement.

anchor.exact: The Recipient/Addressee object is reciprocalized, while the Theme object stays intact.

statement.en: Indirect reciprocals derived from 3-argument verbs reciprocalize the Recipient/Addressee object while leaving the Theme object intact.
statement.ja: 3項動詞から派生した間接相互動詞は、受取手／受託者目的語を相互化し、テーマ目的語をそのまま保持する。

entailment.quote: The Recipient/Addressee object is reciprocalized, while the Theme object stays intact.

anchor.exact: Almost all 3-argument verbs in Ainu are derived (for a single exception see footnote 20) either from applicatives (10b) or causatives (7b).

statement.en: Almost all 3-argument verbs in Ainu are derived either from applicatives or causatives.
statement.ja: アイヌ語の3項動詞のほぼすべては、適用辞または使役辞から派生したものである。

entailment.quote: Almost all 3-argument verbs in Ainu are derived ... either from applicatives ... or causatives.

anchor.exact: There is also a typologically interesting type of object-oriented reciprocal with the meaning of joining sth/sb together. The reciprocals belonging here denote joining, mixing, comparing two or more entities together, and the like.

statement.en: Ainu has object-oriented reciprocals denoting joining, mixing, or comparing together, which take semantically plural objects or coordinated noun phrases.
statement.ja: アイヌ語には、結合・混合・比較を表す目的語指向の相互動詞が存在し、これらは意味的に複数の目的語または並列名詞句をとる。

entailment.quote: There is also a typologically interesting type of object-oriented reciprocal with the meaning of joining sth/sb together. ... The object is always semantically plural or it is expressed by two coordinated nouns

anchor.exact: Ainu seems to lack possessive reflexives proper like ‘test each other’s strength’ or ‘listen to each other’s stories’, but it has a special type of “quasi-possessive” reciprocal, which involve the incorporation of the u- prefixed noun

statement.en: Ainu has quasi-possessive reciprocals that involve incorporating a noun prefixed with the reciprocal marker u- acting as possessor (e.g. u-oruspe-nu 'listen to each other's stories').
statement.ja: アイヌ語には、相互接頭辞u-が所有者として付加された名詞を抱合する「準所有」相互構文が存在する（例：u-oruspe-nu「お互いの話を聞く」）。

entailment.quote: it has a special type of “quasi-possessive” reciprocal, which involve the incorporation of the u- prefixed noun such as u-oruspe ... in u-oruspe-nu

anchor.exact: The reciprocal prefix u- can attach to locative nouns, postpositions, adverbs (cf. sam ‘near’ > u-sam ‘near each other’, tura ‘with sb/sth’ > u-tura ‘with each other, together’, neno ‘like this’ > u-neno ‘like each other, similar to each other’) and body part nouns, but the latter need to be incorporated

statement.en: The reciprocal prefix u- can attach to locative nouns, postpositions, adverbs, and incorporated body-part nouns.
statement.ja: 相互接頭辞u-は位置名詞、後置詞、副詞、および抱合された身体部位名詞に付加することができる。

entailment.quote: The reciprocal prefix u- can attach to locative nouns, postpositions, adverbs ... and body part nouns, but the latter need to be incorporated

anchor.exact: the reflexive prefix is yay-. However, there is also another reflexive prefix, namely si-,as in si-turi-ri ‘stretch oneself’ or si-tuy-tuy-e ‘brush off dust/dirt of oneself’.

statement.en: Ainu has two reflexive prefixes: canonical or direct reflexive yay- and indirect reflexive si-.
statement.ja: アイヌ語には2つの再帰接頭辞、すなわち典型的な直接再帰を表すyay-と間接再帰を表すsi-が存在する。

anchor.exact: In direct reflexive yay-, the subject participates in an action directly, while in indirect reflexive si-, the subject participates in an action only indirectly, i.e., through the involvement of other people.

statement.en: In contrast to direct reflexive yay- where the subject participates directly, indirect reflexive si- encodes that the subject participates in an action only through the involvement of other people.
statement.ja: 主語が直接行為に関与する直接再帰yay-に対し、間接再帰si-は主語が他人の関与を通じてのみ行為に関与することを表す。

anchor.exact: si- . . . -CAUS is regularly used to encode a pretended action in Ainu (Satō 2018).

statement.en: The combination of si- with a causative suffix regularly encodes a pretended or simulative action in Ainu.
statement.ja: アイヌ語において、si-と使尾辞の組み合わせはふりをする行為（見せかけ）を規則的に表す。

anchor.exact: As in the case of reciprocals, both reflexive yay- and si- can attach as possessors to category 1 locative nouns (23), see Nakagawa (Chapter 14, this volume), and body part nouns, to the latter only when they are incorporated.

statement.en: Both reflexive prefixes yay- and si- can attach as possessors to category 1 locative nouns and to incorporated body part nouns.
statement.ja: 再帰接頭辞yay-とsi-の双方は、第1類位置名詞および抱合された身体部位名詞に所有者として付加することができる。

anchor.exact: Bugaeva (2021) argues that it can be regarded as an antipassive marker per se based on its syntactic (eliminating a Patient/Theme/Recipient argument), semantic (denoting an unspecified generic participant or lexicalizing it to a single or subset of objects)

statement.en: The prefix i- functions as an antipassive marker that eliminates a Patient, Theme, or Recipient argument and derives a 1-argument verb from a 2-argument verb.
statement.ja: 接頭辞i-は、被動者・テーマ・受取手項を除去し、2項動詞から1項動詞を派生する逆受動態標識として機能する。

anchor.exact: antipassives from 2-argument verbs result in 1-argument verbs and the original object is obligatorily omitted. It is an S=A type alternation, which is evidenced by the change of the transitive subject indexing (A) to the intransitive subject indexing (S).

statement.en: Antipassivization in Ainu changes transitive subject indexing (A) to intransitive subject indexing (S), and the original object is obligatorily omitted.
statement.ja: アイヌ語の逆受動態化では、他動詞主語の人称標示（A）が自動詞主語の人称標示（S）へと変化し、元の目的語は必須として省略される。

anchor.exact: Antipassives from 3-argument verbs resulting in 2-argument verbs are rather rare, e.g., poyke ‘mix’ (vi) > ko-poyke ‘mix with sth/sb’ (vt) > i-ko-poyke ‘mix with people’ (vi). It is much more common to applicativize antipassives than to antipassivize applicatives

statement.en: Antipassives derived from 3-argument verbs resulting in 2-argument verbs are rare in Ainu, whereas applicativizing an antipassive verb to restore a 2-argument frame is much more common.
statement.ja: アイヌ語において3項動詞から逆受動態化して2項動詞にする派生は稀であり、逆受動態動詞を適用辞化して再び2項動詞にする方がはるかに一般的である。

anchor.exact: it is the Recipient argument that is antipassivized in (25b) and (25c), which is, according to Malchukov, Haspelmath, and Bernard Comrie (2010: 31), extremely rare cross-linguistically. Of course, Ainu perfectly allows antipassivization of the Theme/Patient argument too

statement.en: Ainu permits antipassivization of the Recipient argument as well as the Theme/Patient argument.
statement.ja: アイヌ語ではテーマ／被動者項だけでなく、受取手項の逆受動態化も許容される。

anchor.exact: They are derived from verbs of Perception/ Cognition/ Ingesting/ Interaction/ Communication and Grooming/ Traditional Activities and never from highly transitive verbs of Creation/ Transformation/ Contact by Impact and Effective Action

statement.en: Antipassives in Ainu derive from verbs of perception, cognition, ingesting, interaction, communication, grooming, and traditional activities, but never from highly transitive verbs of creation, transformation, contact by impact, or effective action.
statement.ja: アイヌ語の逆受動態は知覚・認知・摂取・相互行為・伝達・身繕い・伝統的活動を表す動詞から派生し、創造・変形・接触衝撃・効果的動作を表す高他動性動詞からは決して派生しない。

entailment.quote: They are derived from verbs of Perception/ Cognition/ Ingesting/ Interaction/ Communication and Grooming/ Traditional Activities and never from highly transitive verbs of Creation/ Transformation/ Contact by Impact and Effective Action

anchor.exact: The antipassivei- can also be used as an unspecified possessor on obligatorily possessed nouns such as body parts, kinship terms, and locative nouns when they are incorporated as objects of transitive verbs

statement.en: The antipassive prefix i- can serve as an unspecified possessor on obligatorily possessed nouns incorporated as objects of transitive verbs.
statement.ja: 逆受動態接頭辞i-は、他動詞の目的語として抱合された義務的所有名詞において不特定の所有者として機能することができる。

entailment.quote: The antipassivei- can also be used as an unspecified possessor on obligatorily possessed nouns such as body parts, kinship terms, and locative nouns when they are incorporated as objects of transitive verbs

anchor.exact: There are lexical prefixes he- ‘head’ andho- ‘bottom’ originating in nouns, e.g., he-etaye ‘pull one’s head in’ (vi) < etaye ‘pull sth’ (vt), ho-pun-i ‘get up’ (vi) < pun-i ‘raise sth’; they occur immediately before the base.

statement.en: The lexical noun-origin prefixes he- ('head') and ho- ('bottom') attach immediately before the verbal base and reduce verb valency by one.
statement.ja: 名詞起源の語彙接頭辞he-（「頭」）およびho-（「尻」）は動詞語幹の直前に現れ、動詞の結合価を1つ減らす。

entailment.quote: he- ‘head’ and ho- ‘bottom’ originating in nouns, e.g., he-etaye ‘pull one’s head in’ (vi) < etaye ‘pull sth’ (vt), ho-pun-i ‘get up’ (vi) < pun-i ‘raise sth’; they occur immediately before the base
entailment.note: The passage shows valency reduction but does not explicitly state that the effect is always a reduction by exactly one; the examples are one-argument verbs derived from two-argument verbs, which implies reduction of one, but the statement i

anchor.exact: And finally, a few words about the least studied prefix ci-, which can be broadly characterized as ‘middle’ (Tamura 1996: 48). In our corpus (Nakagawa et al. 2016–2021), we have chosen to gloss it an object-resultative marker (RES)

statement.en: The verbal prefix ci- functions as a middle or object-resultative marker.
statement.ja: 動詞接頭辞ci-は中態または目的語結果状態の標識として機能する。

entailment.quote: a few words about the least studied prefix ci-, which can be broadly characterized as ‘middle’ ... we have chosen to gloss it an object-resultative marker (RES)

anchor.exact: The causative suffix -yar/-ar[229] referred to as ‘indefinite’ does not affect valency, which is typologically unusual. There are derivations from both 1-argument as in (30b) and 2-argument verbs (31b)

statement.en: The indefinite causative suffix -yar/-ar retains the valency of the base verb because the causee is only implied and cannot be expressed as an overt NP or personal index.
statement.ja: 不特定使役接尾辞-yar/-arは、被使役者が含意されるのみで名詞句や人称標識として明示できないため、基底動詞の結合価を変化させない（結合価保持的である）。

entailment.quote: The causative suffix -yar/-ar referred to as ‘indefinite’ does not affect valency... the causee is only implied and cannot be encoded with an NP or cross-referenced on the verb

anchor.exact: The suffix -yar/-ar can encode only indirect causation.

statement.en: The indefinite causative suffix -yar/-ar encodes only indirect causation.
statement.ja: 不特定使役接尾辞-yar/-arは間接的使役のみを表す。

entailment.quote: The suffix -yar/-ar can encode only indirect causation

anchor.exact: Synchronically, these ‘with each other’ prefixes were reanalyzed as single sociative markers uko- and uwe-,[231]which do not change valency and add the meaning ‘together’.

statement.en: The sociative prefixes uko- and uwe- originate from combinations of the reciprocal prefix u- with applicatives ko- and e-, and synchronically function as single valency-retaining markers meaning 'together'.
statement.ja: 協調接頭辞uko-およびuwe-は、相互接頭辞u-と適用接頭辞ko-およびe-の結合に由来し、共時的には結合価を変化させずに「一緒に」という意味を付加する単一の標識として機能する。

entailment.quote: these ‘with each other’ prefixes were reanalyzed as single sociative markers uko- and uwe-, which do not change valency and add the meaning ‘together’

anchor.exact: However, there are much more sociative derivations with uko- than with uwe-; that is probably because the comitative function ‘with’ is relatively rare in e- applicatives (and common in ko-)

statement.en: Sociative derivations with uko- are much more frequent than those with uwe-.
statement.ja: uko-による協調接頭辞派生は、uwe-による派生よりもはるかに頻度が高い。

entailment.quote: there are much more sociative derivations with uko- than with uwe-

anchor.exact: There are sociative derivations from 1-argument verbs and 2-argument verbs. The former can only be subject-oriented (36), i.e., the subject is plural, while the latter can be either subject (37) and object-oriented (38)

statement.en: Sociative derivations from 1-argument verbs are exclusively subject-oriented, whereas those from 2-argument verbs can be either subject- or object-oriented depending on context.
statement.ja: 1項動詞からの協調接頭辞派生は専ら主語指向であるのに対し、2項動詞からの派生は文脈に応じて主語指向にも目的語指向にもなりうる。

entailment.quote: The former can only be subject-oriented (36), i.e., the subject is plural, while the latter can be either subject (37) and object-oriented (38), which is determined by the context.

anchor.exact: the sociative meaning can also be expressed by a combination of the reciprocal prefix u- and causative suffixes -re/-e/-te or -ka, literally ‘make each other do sth’, which quite unexpectedly results in ‘together’.

statement.en: The sociative meaning 'together' can also be expressed by combining the reciprocal prefix u- with causative suffixes -re/-e/-te or -ka, mostly on intransitive bases.
statement.ja: 「一緒に」という協調の意味は、相互接頭辞u-と使役接尾辞-re/-e/-teまたは-kaの結合によっても表され、その大部分は自動詞語幹から派生する。

entailment.quote: the sociative meaning can also be expressed by a combination of the reciprocal prefix u- and causative suffixes -re/-e/-te or -ka ... Almost all of these sociatives are derived from intransitive bases

anchor.exact: When these are prefixed to a verb, they fill one noun element required by the verb, but at the same time, they require their own possessors. As a result, the overall valency of the verb does not change.

statement.en: The affiliative form-like prefixes e- ('head of') and o- ('bottom of') satisfy one argument required by the verb but introduce their own possessor requirement, leaving the overall verbal valency unchanged.
statement.ja: 所属形様接頭辞e-（「〜の頭」）およびo-（「〜の尻」）は動詞が要求する1つの項を満たすが、同時に自身の所有者を要求するため、動詞全体の結合価を変化させない。

entailment.quote: When these are prefixed to a verb, they fill one noun element required by the verb, but at the same time, they require their own possessors. As a result, the overall valency of the verb does not change.
